description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2023: Engineering with Nature: How Effective are Hybrid Solutions at Reducing Overtopping? is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Daniel Cox, Oregon State University (oregonstate.edu). My research project was about the potential efficiency of hybrid solutions as coastal protection against wave effects. Mangrove forests were the subject of interest, as we determined their ability to reduce wave overtopping alone, and in a hybrid system with a rock revetment wall. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-ggbj-7h62. Keywords: NHERI HWRL; Mangrove Forests; Overtopping; Large-scale Physical Modeling; O. H. Hinsdale Wave Research Laboratory; Hybrid Solutions; Green and Gray Infrastructure; Engineering with Nature. Published 2023-09-01. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
